On a computing cluster, RiboPilot sends each step of the pipeline to the
cluster's scheduler as a job, and runs the analysis tools in Singularity (or
Apptainer). You still open the app, review results, and export from the app;
only the heavy work runs on compute nodes.

# Choose a profile

A profile tells RiboPilot how to submit jobs on your cluster. Two are built in
and ready to use: `executor = "NMNH_Hydra"` and `executor = "NOAA_SEDNA"`.

For any other Slurm, SGE, PBS, or LSF cluster, make a profile once with
`RiboPilot::generate_config()`, then pass its name to `new_project()`:

```r
RiboPilot::generate_config(
  "mylab_slurm",
  scheduler       = "slurm",
  queue           = "general",
  account         = "mylab",
  walltime        = "48h",
  container_cache = "/scratch/mylab/singularity"
)
RiboPilot::new_project(path = "/shared/mylab/my_project",
  mapping_fn = "/shared/mylab/my_samples.csv",
  data_path = "/shared/mylab/reads", executor = "mylab_slurm")
```

`container_cache` is the folder where Singularity keeps the RiboPilot image,
shared by every project that uses the profile; it must be visible from the
compute nodes. If you leave it out, RiboPilot uses `NXF_SINGULARITY_CACHEDIR`
when that is set, and otherwise a `containers` folder inside your reference
folder. Many clusters need a `walltime`: some reject a job that asks for none.

Profiles are saved in your own settings folder (on Linux,
`~/.config/R/RiboPilot`). To share one with your lab, save it in a shared folder
with `profile_dir`, and pass the same `profile_dir` to `new_project()`:

```r
RiboPilot::generate_config(
  "mylab_slurm",
  scheduler   = "slurm",
  queue       = "general",
  walltime    = "48h",
  profile_dir = "/shared/mylab/ribopilot_profiles"
)
RiboPilot::new_project(
  path        = "/shared/mylab/my_project",
  mapping_fn  = "/shared/mylab/my_samples.csv",
  data_path   = "/shared/mylab/reads",
  executor    = "mylab_slurm",
  profile_dir = "/shared/mylab/ribopilot_profiles"
)
```

# Put everything on shared storage

The project folder, the reads, the reference folder, and the R library that
holds RiboPilot must be visible from the login node and from every compute
node.

# Open the app

On **RStudio Server**, just run `RiboPilot::RiboPilot("/shared/mylab/my_project")`.

Without RStudio Server, start the app on the login node and reach it from your
own computer through an SSH tunnel. On the login node, in R:

```r
RiboPilot::RiboPilot("/shared/mylab/my_project", port = 8123,
                     launch.browser = FALSE)
```

The app prints the address to open and the tunnel command. On your own
computer, in a terminal:

```bash
ssh -N -L 8123:localhost:8123 you@login.cluster.edu
```

Then open http://localhost:8123 in your browser.

When a batch scheduler (sbatch, qsub, or bsub) is on the PATH, or the app runs
on RStudio Server, the run window offers a job script to submit instead of
**Run from App**, and the app prints a note saying so when it starts. Pass `headless = FALSE` to run Nextflow on the machine
that serves the app, or `headless = TRUE` to get job scripts anywhere.

::: {.alert .alert-warning}
**The app has no login.** On a shared login node, other users on that node can
reach its port. Pick an unusual port number, and close the app when you are
done.
:::

# Submit a run as a job

Press **Update**. The run window shows the job script for the Nextflow head job,
which stays small and long-lived: 2 CPUs, 8 GB of memory, and 48 hours, in the
queue and with the account from your profile (on Hydra, it goes to Hydra's
queue for workflow managers). Check the partition, account, walltime, and
memory, and edit the script in the window if you need to. Then press **Submit
as job**, or **Save script** to submit it yourself.

The job runs on its own, so you can close the browser; long runs belong here
rather than in **Run from App**. The window does not follow the job: watch it with your
scheduler's tools (`qstat` on Hydra), and press the
reload button above the table to see new results. The app does not track a
submitted job, so do not start another run for the same project until the job
has finished. If you press **Submit as job** again in the same window, the app
warns you first.

Each submission leaves three kinds of files in the project's `.runs` folder:

- `.runs/jobs/`: the job scripts;
- `.runs/logs/`: the scheduler's log for each job;
- `.runs/nextflow/`: one Nextflow log per run.

Once a job has finished, **Run Reports** in the toolbar shows how it went.

In the Assemble step, **Work Dirs** finds the pipeline's working folders for a
sample, from both app runs and cluster jobs.

# The app needs the container too

The app itself runs the container for two things: the final ITSx check at
export, and the note about the bundled rDNA database in the BLAST Options window. So
Singularity (or Docker) must work on the node where the app runs, and it should
use the same image cache as your jobs, or it downloads the whole image again.

# On the NMNH Hydra cluster

The app sets up Hydra's scheduler and Java for you when it starts. You only need
`RiboPilot::hydra_setup()` when you run the pipeline from the R console. The job
script runs `nextflow` from your PATH, so install Nextflow somewhere `~/.bashrc`
puts on the PATH (for example `~/bin`).

The [Get started](RiboPilot.html) walkthrough marks each place where Hydra
differs, in boxes tagged HYDRA.
